quest.title: Procrustes' Iron Bed
quest.description: The so-called wedding at the House of Hesperides turns out to be less delightful than expected. Pavlina tries to sacrifice Ikor for her wish, though she is fortunately thwarted by Aksinya in the end. Pavlina is also thrown into the Shadow Realm, where she will continue to face off with Aksinya...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #...{NICKNAME}... {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew — there you are! Did the bell wake you? You were completely out. Is the bed here really that comfy?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think I had a dream.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No wonder. You were asleep for a long time. Paimon's been keeping watch the whole while. Was it a nice dream, or a scary one?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, never mind. Tell Paimon later. Now's not really the time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you remember what happened earlier? We came to the House of Hesperides for a wedding.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But that "ritual" wasn't a wedding at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That towering princess of the Snegurochka, Pavlina... She nearly killed Ikor...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon knows Ikor isn't really human, strictly speaking. He's just a fragment of the power that originally belonged to Goggles. But even so...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: Compassion is something to be respected, Miss Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They've been carrying out this "ritual" again and again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thanks, Goggles. When Pavlina cast her spell, Goggles was the one who protected us and brought us here, somewhere safe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: While you were asleep, Paimon did some poking around. Looks like someone named Myshkin used to live here. Didn't Aglaya mention him when she first welcomed us?

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: ...*cough* Hello? Do you copy? You should be able to hear what I'm saying, I think.

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: *sigh* Thanks for nothing, you two. I poured so much effort into getting "him" out, even if in part... Only for you to send him right back, as if nothing had happened. Pavlina almost won right there and then.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh? You're...

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: ...Hmm. It's been a while since we last met, eh, dear colleague? Don't you think you're getting "a bit too passionate" right now?

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: Ah, sorry, that wasn't meant for you. I'm currently busy dealing with that crazy shrew... How tragic, Pavlina of the Snegovik. You've completely lost it.

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: Her gaze is like Prime Ice, but her mind is like a powderkeg. A single spark could set her off and destroy all around her.

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: In any case, I know what you want. We have the same goal.

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: I've trapped Pavlina, but have little time for anything else right now. Take "his" fragments away from here, one by one, while she's weakened by being in this area, away from her grasp.

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: This mansion... I came here often in the past... I shall provide you with the map in a while.

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: Get moving. I won't be able to hold out for long. Finish your business before the clock strikes eight times. Before the wedding, or perhaps everything else, starts all over again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello??? Hello...? She's gone...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Take Goggles' fragments... one by one? What does she even mean? Doesn't she know that Pavlina has some of Goggles' power too???

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She may have something else up her sleeves too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... Better take what she says with a huge rock of salt. But what should we do now then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, you know what? This is about Goggles! We should ask what he wants.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: I think... Maybe we should gather at least some of the power that has been split up, and try to make him as complete as possible. Then we can take it all back.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: This may sound a little ironic, but my wish is for the fragments, incomplete as they are, to be as whole as possible...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: It's just like how the Snegurochka princess must have decided to perform the ritual because she wanted to help her people become more "whole."

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: And that is something I can understand, and even empathize with, to some degree.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How can you feel for her!? She was gonna gobble you up, piece by piece, just to get what she wanted!!!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can share her food or Mora with other folks, no problem. But if you want Paimon to hand over an arm or a leg...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Or even Paimon's hair! Hmm... Actually, hair seems alright... especially if it's just a few strands — Anyway, that's not the point.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It doesn't matter what the other person's reasons are. This is something... something Paimon needs to think over! Very carefully! Though Paimon probably won't say yes anyway, to be honest...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes. It's not good to over-deplete yourself for the sake of others.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: ...You are right. But that aside, there is another reason we must reclaim him "whole."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Another reason? And what would that be?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That you don't need to know, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Are the two of you keeping something from Paimon!? And Paimon's not talking about secret snack stashes or anything like tha——

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We should get moving.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: I have marked the fragment locations. Let's go, before the clock strikes eight.

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: Who are you people? And what are you doing here in this room?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? You must be Aglaya. We, uh, we've already shown our invite earlier...

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: Is that so? But how do you know my name...? Ah, you must have heard it from the others.

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: Alright then. I'm guessing someone has already told you about the dos and don'ts around here.

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: But this room is... also off-limits... Ahem. This isn't a room for ordinary guests.

dialogues.speaker: Aglaia
dialogues.text: The ritual will begin when <color=#00E1FFFF>the clock strikes eight times</color>. I wish the both of you a most pleasant and unforgettable day here at the House of Hesperides.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Aglaya leaves...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The way she was acting, it was like she had never met us before... That's weird. Is it because... everything has restarted?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you okay? How do you feel now?

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: He may have a body now, but he is still only a puppet. He cannot feel anything so complex, nor can he answer you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon knows, but still... It's not like it hurts to ask. Just let Paimon be.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: Like I said before, your compassion is something to be respected. That kindness is one of your virtues.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: #But I don't think {NICKNAME} would want it to end up hurting you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you mean...? Wait, does this have something to do with what you were all hiding from Paimon earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: You... really are an odd one. You are me. But it's something I've only realized today.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: That is because my presence has become more evident now that the princess is no longer in the way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How does it feel to converse with yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: More ordinary than I'd ever imagined. Even if I was fortunate enough to have a body right now, I doubt we'd be throwing our arms around each other and crying.

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: This body won't shed a tear, for it is created out of Prime Ice.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: Yes. That, I am aware.

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: Ah, that's right. You may not possess form, but you have something that I don't... reason and intelligence.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, could we pick up this conversation again a little later? We've got to get somewhere safe now. Who knows when Pavlina is coming back...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Although, she still has one of the fragments with her... That's right. What are we gonna do about that fragment?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do we talk her out of the ritual? That doesn't seem very possible... She hasn't exactly been open to persuasion so far.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Is defeating her the only way then? Not that Paimon doesn't have trust in {NICKNAME} or anything...

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: ...Do you seek to stop the ritual?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mmhmm! If that ritual continues, you'll be finished! Finito! Dunzo!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon knows that you're not really human, and your uh, form of existence is different from ours. But we cannot possibly sit back and watch you get wiped out by her.

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: I apologize, but I'm afraid I cannot assist with this wish of yours.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why?

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: The ritual has long been set in motion. Though the taboo that must not be inquired into or spoken of has already been broken, the ritual has fallen into distortion... It can neither be halted nor reversed.

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: The only course remaining to me is to become one with it... or fade entirely into the ether.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!?!? But without you, Goggles will never be whole again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But if the ritual were to continue...

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: This is neither death nor the end. It is a return, a birth. If all goes well, all the Snegovik under her protection will receive a new lease of life.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is that what you really believe, or what she made you believe?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y—Yeah... Paimon remembers how you never pushed back on anything, not even once, when we first met you. Are you sure she didn't put this idea in your head, too?

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: Strangely, my mind feels remarkably clear at present, and I find myself recalling certain things from the past.

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: We were once companions who shared the same ambition... And we were willing to pay the price for a love set free, for the sake of that "more perfect world" of her dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: Of course, it is natural that one pays a price for their dreams to come true. Yet even if you have finally made your choice, the path ahead will not be an easy one either.

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: And eventually, she simply disappeared somewhere along the way, among the countless refinements and ascensions...

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: She had even forgotten that I once chose to do all of this, without need of shackles.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: ...You do know that you will not succeed.

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: I have neither your reason nor your intelligence, and I cannot predict things that have yet to happen.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that the thing you were reluctant to tell Paimon??? That's ridiculous... Are you sure there's no other way?

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: Just as the dew upon leaf and flower inevitably finds its way back to the stream, so too is the path toward becoming one irreversible. Once a single drop has returned to the waters, there is no way it can be reclaimed.

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: But nevertheless, I thank you for your... consideration. I now understand why the other "me" chose to travel with you.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: ...Hey! I do hope the two of you have sent out the fragments like I said, since I am in quite the predicament now myself.

dialogues.speaker: Aksinya
dialogues.text: I'm trapped here, and shall have to be away for a while... That was quite the move. I will leave the rest to you.

dialogues.speaker: Ikor
dialogues.text: I should go now. She's here for me.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
"The bell tolls again."
You hear a cold voice say:
"No matter how many times this happens, you cannot stop it..."
"You cannot stop any of it..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #...{NICKNAME}... {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're in a loop...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mm... are we...? Ah... right...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, Paimon's head suddenly feels so fuzzy... But if we're awake again, then...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: Then the ritual isn't finished yet.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: Miss Aksinya is still holding Pavlina off for now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then we'd better hurry. We need to get that fragment back before Pavlina gets here.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
"The bell tolls again."
You hear a cold voice say:
"No matter how many times this happens, you cannot stop it..."
"You cannot stop any of it..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #...{NICKNAME}... {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew — there you are! Did the bell wake you? You were completely out. Is the bed here really that comfy?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No, Paimon... We've already been through this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh... right. Paimon knew this felt familiar...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, Paimon remembers now. The bell rang eight times... and then we...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: Wound up right back here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Goggles...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: It is the ritual taking place here... It repeats over and over...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: Until Pavlina, princess of the Snegurochka, has drained every last bit of power from the fragment of my body.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then, does that mean she's already completed the ritual? Are we too late?

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: ...Have you not succeeded yet?

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: Seems I'll have to hold on a little longer... It seems Pavlina does not need to maintain the ritual that causes the mansion to loop...

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: The good news is... that any ritual she does not perform will not result in a "full restoration." Things that you modified in a previous cycle cannot be wholly reset...

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: Similarly, she could not absorb any power from that last cycle... We do happen to be evenly matched within the Shadow Realm at the moment, after all...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So I suppose we're not too late?

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: ...Not this time, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: Still, I cannot say how much longer I can last. Three cycles? Four?

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: Before I... Before my strength fails, you must... *sigh* Time runs short.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... looks like the ritual isn't over yet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go get that fragment back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It rang eight times... But Pavlina still hasn't gotten free, has she? There's no way that "ritual" can start again...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: Even so, the last piece we need is in the assembly hall. Whatever happens...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mm... You're right. We can't afford to hesitate. Let's go to the assembly hall.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: The "ritual" is not yet complete. We must defeat her before it is finished and remove the fragment from her.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: But before that, it seems we must first deal with the matter at hand.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: The final location of the "ritual" has been marked for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... The Snegovik are trying to stop us from chasing Pavlina...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've gotta take them down first!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There he is! Thank goodness, we got to him before Pavlina did...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #...{NICKNAME}... {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew — there you are! Did the bell wake you? You were completely out. Is the bed here really that comfy?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think I had a dream.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No wonder. You were asleep for a long time. Paimon's been keeping watch the whole while. Was it a nice dream, or a scary one?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, never mind. Tell Paimon later. Now's not really the time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you remember what happened earlier? We came to the House of Hesperides for a wedding.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But that "ritual" wasn't a wedding at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That towering princess of the Snegurochka, Pavlina... She nearly killed Ikor...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon knows Ikor isn't really human, strictly speaking. He's just a fragment of the power that originally belonged to Goggles. But even so...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: Compassion is something to be respected, Miss Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They've been carrying out this "ritual" again and again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is... is that what was happening?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's what you saw in your dream?

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}... please stay calm. This is to be expected. Pavlina is a fae, after all... She can't draw all the power from my body fragment at once.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: So she has to do it bit by bit, through the ritual again and again... That's what the Snegovik's ritual is: they take a soul from someone they love, to make themselves whole.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: ...Snegovik are fae created without flesh and blood, and thus their souls are incomplete.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Snegovik are fae born for love...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: Rather, they are fae who can only become whole through love... by taking another's soul.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: ...That is why so many love stories centered on Snegovik end in tragedy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How could that happen? Thank goodness... Actually, thank goodness Goggles was there. We never would've made it out of that wedding without him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thanks, Goggles. When Pavlina cast her spell, Goggles was the one who protected us and brought us here, somewhere safe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: While you were asleep, Paimon did some poking around. Looks like someone named Myshkin used to live here. Didn't Aglaya mention him when she first welcomed us?

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: ...*cough* Hello? Do you copy? You should be able to hear what I'm saying?

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: *sigh* Thanks for nothing, you two. I poured so much effort into getting "him" out, even if in part... Only for you to send him right back, as if nothing had happened. Pavlina almost won right there and then.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh? Aksinya?

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: Ha! I am the creator of the Eye of Graeae, after all. I can still make use of some of its functions.

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: ...Hmm. It's been a while since we last met, eh, dear colleague? Don't you think you're getting "a bit too passionate" right now?

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: Ah, sorry, that wasn't meant for you. I'm currently busy dealing with that crazy shrew... How tragic, Pavlina of the Snegovik. You've completely lost it.

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: Her gaze is like Prime Ice, but her mind is like a powderkeg. A single spark could set her off and destroy all around her.

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: I've trapped Pavlina, but have little time for anything else right now. Take "his" fragments away from here, one by one, while she's weakened by being in this area, away from her grasp.

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: That's the only way to ensure that shrew won't be able to offer up "his" power for her people.

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: We have to take back all that power, don't we? It's not the same as why she seeks your power, is it? "To have a body once more"... that's what "he" wants, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: Then go. This mansion... I came here often in the past... I shall provide you with the map in a while.

dialogues.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
dialogues.text: Get moving. I won't be able to hold out for long. Finish your business before the clock strikes eight times. Before the wedding, or perhaps everything else, starts all over again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She's gone. Again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Take Goggles' fragments... one by one? What does she even mean? Doesn't she know that Pavlina has some of Goggles' power too???

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She may have something else up her sleeves too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... Better take what she says with a huge rock of salt. But what should we do now then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, you know what? This is about Goggles! We should ask what he wants.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: I think... Maybe we should gather at least some of the power that has been split up, and try to make him as complete as possible. Then we can take it all back.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: This may sound a little ironic, but my wish is for the fragments, incomplete as they are, to be as whole as possible...

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: It's just like how the Snegurochka princess must have decided to perform the ritual because she wanted to help her people become more "whole."

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: And that is something I can understand, and even empathize with, to some degree.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How can you feel for her!? She was gonna gobble you up, piece by piece, just to get what she wanted!!!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can share her food or Mora with other folks, no problem. But if you want Paimon to hand over an arm or a leg...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Or even Paimon's hair! Hmm... Actually, hair seems alright... especially if it's just a few strands—— Anyway, that's not the point.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It doesn't matter what the other person's reasons are. This is something... something Paimon needs to think over! Very carefully! Though Paimon probably won't say yes anyway, to be honest...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes. It's not good to over-deplete yourself for the sake of others.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: ...You are right. But that aside, there is another reason we must reclaim him "whole."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Another reason? And what would that be?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That you don't need to know, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Are the two of you keeping something from Paimon!? And Paimon's not talking about secret snack stashes or anything like tha——

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We should get moving.

dialogues.speaker: Eye of Graeae
dialogues.text: I have marked the fragment locations. Let's go, before the clock strikes eight.
